title: Native clean-profile build and launch baseline
what: A developer can reproducibly build and launch the native reader against an isolated acceptance profile without altering an installed NNW profile.
acceptance: Provide a bounded reproducible macOS build/test entry using installed Xcode; avoid mandatory private upstream secrets or interactive setup for local acceptance.
Native app launch has its own development identity/profile; existing accounts and data in installed NNW remain untouched.
Existing package tests and applicable build/typecheck evidence are recorded, with original failures distinguished from new ones.
Document signing/CloudKit entitlement and simulator prerequisites without inventing a team ID; do not weaken release security to obtain a green local build.

title: Lossless IO snapshot, manifest and independent restore
what: An owner can create a consistent IO database-and-assets snapshot and restore it into an empty destination with a verifiable manifest before a native cutover.
acceptance: Use SQLite backup semantics for WAL/live-source consistency; source originals are never modified or removed.
An executable public snapshot/verify/restore interface preserves every table/row and required asset with version, identity, integrity/count/hash evidence; it rejects incomplete or tampered input.
Interrupted/repeated restore is safe and an existing destination is never silently overwritten.
Synthetic fixtures exercise real source schema and complete round-trip restore; first ticket must not read personal body content, credentials or operate production writes.
Record unsupported legacy forms explicitly rather than dropping them.

title: App-managed IO engine with native health and shutdown
what: The native app starts and stops a private IO processing component and shows its real availability without requiring a separately deployed personal backend.
acceptance: Use existing IO observable contracts and sanitized reusable source where possible; no unrelated FreshRSS runtime requirement.
Provide authenticated private command/read communication, app-managed data locations and lifecycle/error recovery.
Native status differentiates launching, ready, failed and stopped; merely displaying a stub is insufficient.
No personal paths, account identifiers, keys or acceptance-only gates are embedded in public shipping code.
Packaging declares Python/native dependencies and licensing; an actual installed-bundle smoke check proves runtime discovery.

title: BYO AI and Magpie prompt-model configuration
what: A reader configures a service and creates reusable Curator/Editor prompts that explicitly bind a model or gateway target.
acceptance: Native Settings store secrets securely and validate nonsecret endpoint/target configuration; directory refresh performs no inference.
Prompt create/edit/copy/rename/delete and references are functional; Curator and Editor are independently composable.
Each prompt binds its service/target; no hidden inheritance, mandatory Kit pairing or per-feed model override.
Invalid target/authentication/output errors remain distinct and never become zero scores or silent alternate providers.
Magpie requested target and actual/reported model provenance remain separate; sharing instructions excludes secrets.

Prompt history can be browsed and a prior version restored as a new current version; supported input placeholders and legacy aliases remain valid, while unknown placeholders fail before a model request.

title: NNW article identity bridge and configurable feed policies
what: A native subscription can be mapped to IO observations and configured for media, prompts, threshold and automation, including batch source settings.
acceptance: NNW articles/account/feed identities map to stable IO canonical content without changing read/star semantics.
Five media policies, disabled/normal/Important behavior and current scope rules are retained and configurable; a new feed does not start history processing.
One content can retain prompt-context results without duplicating shared human decisions; historical context is preserved.
Shared setting changes disclose affected sources; job snapshots stay coherent and historical rerun requires explicit preview.
An article appears in the native list with actual bridge data, not a separate reader.

title: News acquisition and Curator in native article detail
what: A news article obtains validated body text and displays a real Curator result in NoNews, with access failures recoverable.
acceptance: Existing full-text-before-scoring and same-material binding are preserved.
Access barriers, runtime absence, timeouts and fallback/manual-required routes remain distinct.
Score/title/reason and user prompt output are validated and visible; missing evidence is not a low score.
Fixtures prove material identity and no unauthorized browser/session use; actual native rendering is exercised.

title: Verified paper abstracts and Curator
what: A paper displays identity-validated abstract-based Curator output or an honest missing/candidate/error state.
acceptance: Publisher/arXiv/catalog routes retain existing identity/completeness/provenance validation and available/candidate/missing distinctions.
No full-text fallback silently replaces a missing abstract for scoring; title-only and correction rules retain source behavior.
Native Abstract and Curator layers show the right material and result.
Regression fixtures include mismatched DOI/title, truncated abstract and valid identity.

title: Paper full text, fidelity and eligible acquisition
what: An eligible paper obtains verified full text/PDF/converted content and can be read with equations, figures and references in NoNews.
acceptance: Preserve manual/new-threshold/Important eligibility and Reject precedence; old scores do not silently restart history.
HTML/PDF/OCR routing, material distinctions, coverage verification and explicit manual-required behavior remain.
Native full-text rendering supports formulas/tables/images/footnotes and honest conversion failures.
Input authorization and validated-body checks remain for manual reruns as well as automation.

title: Newsletter acquisition and native reading
what: An input newsletter issue retains full text and ordered links and can be processed/read as one content item.
acceptance: Complete feed issue vs webpage fallback behavior matches IO.
Thin snapshots do not authorize downstream AI; no automatic link-to-independent-item fanout is invented.
Material provenance and useful error states are shown in the shared native detail.

title: Podcast description-to-transcript workflow
what: A podcast is screened from valid description material, then obtains an eligible transcript for processing and native reading.
acceptance: Official show notes and existing RSS fallback preserve current screening rules.
Transcript acquisition follows selection/Important and material gates; missing/short/manual-required states remain explicit.
No automatic ASR or media download is added to claim parity.
Native layers distinguish description, transcript and source audio link.

title: Video description-to-captions workflow
what: A video retains description-based judgment and eligible explicit transcript/caption reading inside the native article.
acceptance: Explicit transcript URLs and validated supported API captions preserve current behavior.
Unsupported/missing subtitles are manual-required, not an empty successful transcript.
No new yt-dlp, video understanding or ASR dependency is invented.
Native article exposes actual materials/source link and failures.

title: Automatic and manual Editor with immutable draft versions
what: A reader receives an Editor draft via configured automation or explicit action and can rerun, inspect and compare versions.
acceptance: Preserve threshold/Important/manual eligibility, source snapshots, current validation and actual model/material provenance.
Output contract remains media-appropriate; failed retries preserve previous successful drafts.
Native Draft detail supports versions, compare, explicit regenerate and protected-version deletion rules.
No new draft test-run feature or conversational editor is introduced.

title: Integrated native Curator, Draft and material reading
what: A reader uses a single NNW detail with Curator/Draft/material tabs and native keyboard/window behavior.
acceptance: First available evaluation opens Curator; use current IO prompt-result presentation without forced extra metadata.
Preserve Abstract for papers, Fulltext/Original distinctions and unavailable-material/error states.
Keep IO list content and requested sorting; do not add rejected Draft list preview.
Responsive native column layout, themes/font sizes, web-content safety and keyboard focus remain coherent.
No new Continue deeper gate or mandatory fold hierarchy.

title: Yep/Nope decisions, undo and configurable side effects
what: A reader can decide without AI prerequisites, undo, and safely stop or continue processing according to explicit settings.
acceptance: Yep stays; Nope advances only within current results and handles end-of-list; Star/read are independent.
Preserve command intent/audit and duplicate observations; do not train recommendations.
Nope invalidates pending/late work authorization; cleanup preference is surfaced without weakening protected-reference checks.
Undo/restoration has real public behavior and native keyboard/buttons/gestures with accessible labels.
Integration linkage is configurable; a decision alone is never reported as external success.

title: IO filters, dates and Quick views in NNW
what: A reader combines existing IO filters, sees/removes conditions and saves/reuses Quick views in the same native reader.
acceptance: Preserve AI/human/read/Star/publication conditions, date controls and native search scope.
English Your decision values All/Undecided/Yep/Nope; save/apply/delete Quick views persists.
Do not create custom Smart Feed editor or expand Quick view scope beyond agreed IO behavior.
Query and result counts match the actual full scope, with unsupported advanced predicates preserved rather than flattened.

title: Full-result batch preview and processing
what: A power user previews and commits batch decisions/reprocessing against selected articles or complete filtered results.
acceptance: Preview pins successful decisions, query scope, policy distribution and phase estimates without enqueueing work.
Commit skips reviewed/duplicate/ineligible items and refuses changed routing until re-previewed.
Accept AI, process current results and explicit historical reprocessing retain distinct collection semantics.
Native selection, progress, undo/cancel and error reporting are functional.

title: Configurable Zotero collection and existing-work protection
what: A reader collects supported media into a configured Zotero target with existing ownership safeguards and verified status.
acceptance: Preserve explicit intent eligibility; auto high score and Accept AI alone do not become collection commands.
Correct media parents/attachments/notes and identity resolution retain current behavior.
Never overwrite user notes/annotations or claim a near-title record; external target and optional Yep linkage are configurable.
Native status separates decision, queued/failed collection and readback-confirmed success.
Fixtures prove idempotency/ownership; live isolated readback evidence is reported separately.

title: Obsidian personal reading copies and helper continuity
what: A reader explicitly creates/opens an Obsidian working copy without overwriting personal edits and can keep the existing Zotero helper path.
acceptance: Configured vault/paths replace personal hardcodes; existing native action/helper compatibility remains.
Missing body creates no empty note; repeat exports protect user modifications; explicit rebuild handles missing files.
Navigation-only badges do not auto-create files; Zotero full-text linkage is verified where applicable.
Native action and helper round-trip are tested at the public integration boundary.

title: Issue adoption, usage and external receipt reconciliation
what: An editor adopts a specific News/Paper draft into a configured existing issue and can verify usage across existing external workflows.
acceptance: Preserve eligible existing issue selection and draft/image/type gates; do not create issues implicitly or equate adoption with public publishing.
Intent/receipt pins canonical content/version/issue identity, avoids duplicate blocks and requires explicit hash-checked replacement.
External macros/spool/catch-up update the shared ledger without importing private body text into status records.
Native status shows pending/verified/unknown appropriately; new drafts never silently overwrite adopted versions.

title: Readable images, configured upload and repair
what: A reader sees material/draft images and can recover failed local resolution or configured uploads.
acceptance: Local image lookup and optional upload/staging/receipt retain provenance and trust boundaries.
Private source assets are not automatically published; public image targets are explicit settings.
Native content displays useful missing-image state and repair action; retries are idempotent.

title: Native Activity, attention and processing controls
what: A user views real jobs, failures and history and can change processing capacity or retry/cancel at the correct scope.
acceptance: Preserve Jobs/Needs attention/History, failure grouping, same-cause retry, dismiss and resolved-history semantics.
Worker limits/current scope are configurable; cancel queued does not falsely claim to kill running work.
Health/worker presence is not reported as end-to-end integration success; 400-row windows are not global totals.
Service errors do not interrupt ordinary NNW reading or leak request bodies/secrets.

title: IO lifecycle, version ownership and recoverable cleanup
what: An owner uses existing IO retention/recovery behavior safely alongside NNW cache cleanup and can configure personal cleanup preferences.
acceptance: Existing database/file-authority boundaries, immutable versions and checksum checks remain; NNW article eviction cannot silently delete IO evidence.
Preserve seven-day reject recovery and Select rescue when enabled, protected references and independent backup-readback requirements.
Storage settings explain scope; cleanup leaves required identity/audit/tombstones, and external copies are not blindly deleted.
Restore/failed-cleanup/late-write scenarios are verifiable through public operations.

title: Historical catalog, scopes and advanced maintenance
what: An advanced user can continue the current history discovery, import, reconciliation and repair workflows from supported configurable tools.
acceptance: Preserve journal/arXiv/conference discovery, scope/time-window/import and dedup capabilities without claiming unimplemented coverage.
Personal source/time/vault constants become settings; unsupported forms are explicit.
Advanced native command/tool entry executes actual operations with preview/progress/restore evidence.
Normal reading is not forced through maintenance setup; no capability is dropped because it is advanced.

title: Configurable classification and source value statistics
what: A user can configure valid topic/classification vocabularies and inspect existing source value metrics from native settings/Inspector.
acceptance: Preserve Paper label validation and News classification capabilities without forcing personal research categories.
Source 30/90/all-time reviewed/selected/star/value-density metrics preserve distinct-content counting and IO formulas.
NNW Star semantics and user labels stay intact; statistics do not auto-unsubscribe, rank or train recommendations.
Native source settings/Inspector expose useful results with empty and unavailable states.

title: Persistent two-client IO sync and offline convergence
what: Two separately stored clients synchronize IO settings, decisions and result references with durable retry and deterministic merge behavior.
acceptance: Use stable content/context identities; preserve versions/intents/receipts and protected assets without secret synchronization in ordinary records.
Offline outbox, acknowledgments, conflicts, deletions/tombstones and duplicate delivery converge and survive restart.
Reject precedence and adopted-version protection survive delayed remote operations; do not duplicate paid work on replay.
Tests exercise actual persistent public adapters; fake transport tests are labeled separately from cloud verification.

title: NNW-compatible CloudKit transport and macOS sync UI
what: A configured owner synchronizes IO data between native Mac clients with a supported transport and can understand account/offline failures.
acceptance: Inspect/reuse suitable NNW CloudKit sync seams; custom IO state must not piggyback unsupported third-party RSS fields.
App entitlements/container/signing requirements and privacy are explicit; keep original account/read/star sync operational.
Native Settings show enabling/state/error/retry, not a switch backed only by local storage.
Transport works with real authorized accounts for acceptance; signed-out/local accounts have honest non-synced status.
Actual draft/material availability and asset transfers are verified, not metadata-only claims.

title: iOS consumption and synchronized IO decision continuity
what: An iPhone running the shared app can resume synchronized Curator/Draft/material reading and judgments while preserving NNW mobile behavior.
acceptance: Shared sync records/settings/results and Yep/Nope are consumed with real account boundary handling.
iOS build remains green; native navigation, safe areas, text scaling and accessibility match Apple conventions.
Missing/offline assets are explicit; no device pretends that reading metadata proves complete content transfer.
Two-client/device continuity and original read/star sync are evidenced; unavailable physical-account checks remain pending.

title: Full personal database migration and native cutover
what: The existing owner imports the entire verified IO database/assets/configuration, maps sources and resumes the complete workflow in NoNews.
acceptance: Native importer previews the complete snapshot and destination/source mappings, validates version/integrity/space and reports every retained/unmapped asset.
All rows, histories, versions, decisions, settings, bindings, jobs, collection/adoption/receipts and legacy references are accounted for; no sample-only substitute.
Historical import is passive: no model runs, collection or adoption replay without explicit post-import action.
Full private-data reconciliation and independent restore evidence are local/redacted; source system remains intact and rollback demonstrable.
Resumed native workflow is exercised against actual authorized services without overwriting existing personal work.

title: First-use setup and coherent configurable settings
what: A new user independently connects AI, creates/reuses prompts and configures sources/integrations through understandable native settings.
acceptance: Basic reading works without any AI; no terminal/deployment dependency or mandatory conversational onboarding.
Group personal preferences by task; clear defaults/impact/scope, copy choices and unavailable state recovery retain all powers.
Direct-model and Magpie users see accurate connection/target provenance; no prompt trial-run or silent paid health call.
Observed first-use task script records misunderstandings and fixes material friction, rather than just asserting fields exist.

title: NNW-native Liquid Glass and accessible UX finish
what: The complete native reading and configuration journey is visually and behaviorally consistent with NNW and Apple HIG.
acceptance: Use standard AppKit/UIKit controls, semantic colors/SF Symbols and native Liquid Glass where supported; readable content avoids decorative glass.
Verify light/dark, narrow/wide windows, keyboard focus/shortcuts, VoiceOver and Reduce Motion/Transparency; supported older OS has native fallback.
One batched Impeccable inspection, one correction batch and at most one confirmation per target; fix material task-blocking/native violations.
Capture fresh native evidence tied to commit/device/appearance and actual behavior; source-only review is not visual acceptance.
No extra Draft previews, forced integration-after-reading gate or new workspaces appear as visual scope creep.

title: Full parity acceptance, migration/sync readback and release handoff
what: The owner can use all prior IO abilities in NoNews and a new user can independently configure the product, backed by final parity evidence.
acceptance: Every active capability and newly discovered active source behavior has an accepted ticket plus meaningful test/runtime evidence; retired items are honestly separated.
Run full appropriate macOS/iOS builds and tests, integration/migration/sync live readback and independently aggregated Standards/Spec reviews.
No material code/UX/accessibility/data-integrity issue remains; private final evidence is locally accessible with redacted public summary.
Each completed ticket has commit and remote ref, review base/HEAD and test outcome; goal is not completed while live prerequisites remain pending.
Clean abandoned changes and deliver runnable app, migration/rollback guide and known limitations without award claims.
